entries.title: The whole sidecar (including the unauthenticated /mcp surface with 36 tools, invoke_agent among them) answers any browser Origin with access-control-allow-origin: * and performs no Origin validation
entries.repro: Against the isolated R15 sidecar: `curl -i -X OPTIONS http://127.0.0.1:52152/mcp/ -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type'` -> 200 with `access-control-allow-origin: *`; then `curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:52152/mcp/ -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"x","version":"0"}}}'` -> 200, `access-control-allow-origin: *`, full capability handshake. `grep -n 'Origin' sidecar/app.py sidecar/services/mcp_server.py sidecar/routers/mcp.py` returns no hits.
entries.evidence: sidecar/app.py:301, sidecar/app.py:303, sidecar/app.py:345, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:377, sidecar/routers/mcp.py:14 || refuter: COD-mcp-servers-1: refuter admitted_with_correction -> high
entries.root_cause: app.py:301-303 installs CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=['*'], allow_methods=['*']) app-wide and nothing checks Origin; routers/mcp.py:13-14 justifies no auth by the 127.0.0.1 bind, which is exactly the assumption MCP's Origin-validation requirement defends against (browser pages reaching localhost).
entries.fix_shape: Replace the wildcard with an explicit allow-list (tauri://localhost, http://tauri.localhost, the dev vite origin) and reject a present-but-unlisted Origin with 403 before routing (covers /mcp and every REST route). Pin with a TestClient test: Origin https://evil.example -> 403 on POST /mcp/ and on a REST GET; tauri origin -> 200. Note: does not defend against local processes (they send no Origin).

entries.title: A dead openbb-mcp / sec-edgar-mcp child stalls the first call 60 s and the next call escapes as asyncio.CancelledError, so the provider registry does not fall through to yfinance for that request (reconnect except-tuple narrower than documented)
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: build `c = mcp_client.McpClient('t', transport='http', endpoint='http://x/mcp')`, set `c._session` to a stub whose `call_tool` raises each of anyio.ClosedResourceError / anyio.BrokenResourceError / httpx.ReadError, then `await c.call_tool('t', {})`. Result: `ClosedResourceError session dropped? False`, `BrokenResourceError session dropped? False`, `ReadError session dropped? False` (expected True). Verified against the installed venv that none of anyio.ClosedResourceError, anyio.BrokenResourceError, anyio.EndOfStream, httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadError, httpx.RemoteProtocolError is an OSError subclass (anyio 4.13.0, httpx 0.28.1, mcp 1.27.1).
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_client.py:158, sidecar/services/mcp_client.py:182, sidecar/services/mcp_client.py:15, sidecar/tests/test_mcp_client.py:114, sidecar/tests/test_mcp_client.py:124 || refuter: COD-mcp-servers-2: refuter admitted_with_correction -> medium || severity note: Raw said high ('cached until app restart'); refuter disproved that headline by experiment and restated the real defect, medium.
entries.root_cause: mcp_client.py:158/182 catch only (TimeoutError, McpError, OSError); the refuter's kill/restart experiment showed the SDK surfaces a dead server as McpError after a 60 s read timeout (caught, session dropped), but the following call raises CancelledError from the dead transport's task group, which is neither caught there nor a ProviderError in _call_tool, so the registry fallback is skipped.
entries.fix_shape: In McpClient.call_tool/list_tools catch Exception (re-raising only a genuine outer-task cancellation) and convert transport-origin CancelledError/anyio/httpx errors into ProviderError after dropping the session; shorten the per-call read timeout for local children or gate on a port probe. Test: parametrise test_mcp_client.py:114 over anyio.ClosedResourceError, httpx.ReadError and a transport CancelledError and assert the session is dropped and a ProviderError is raised.

entries.title: Key validation lies for three of eight providers: a typo'd/revoked OpenRouter key is reported valid and saved to the keychain; a bad Gemini/xAI key is reported as a 'transport error' and misses the chat stream's key-rejected message
entries.repro: get_provider('openrouter').validate_key('not-a-real-key') -> True (live call; openrouter.ai/api/v1/models answers 200 with or without auth, while /api/v1/key answers 401 'User not found.' for the same key). get_provider('gemini').validate_key('AIzaSyNOTAREALKEY...') -> raises ClientError 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT 'API key not valid' -> POST /llm/keys/validate returns ok=false detail='transport error: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. {...}'. curl api.x.ai/v1/models with a fake bearer -> HTTP 400 {"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Incorrect API key provided..."} -> openai.BadRequestError, not AuthenticationError -> same 'transport error' path.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:842-855, sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:186-204, sidecar/routers/llm.py:99-111, src/components/KeyEntryDialog.tsx:64-82, sidecar/services/errors.py:165-171, sidecar/services/llm/base.py:109-118 || refuter: COD-llm-adapters-2-4: refuter admitted -> medium

entries.title: Gemini usage omits thinking and grounding-prompt tokens, so BudgetGuard under-meters every thinking Gemini round and a Delegate run can overspend past its USD/token ceiling
entries.repro: Gemini 2.5 Pro round that thinks 6k tokens and answers 800 -> usage_metadata.candidates_token_count=800, thoughts_token_count=6000 -> adapter reports output_tokens=800 -> BudgetGuard.record folds 800 + input; the user's key is billed for 6800 output tokens.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:167-173, sidecar/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/google/genai/types.py:7796-7826 (total_token_count 'is the sum of prompt_token_count, candidates_token_count, tool_use_prompt_token_count, and thoughts_token_count'), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:116-133, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking.md.txt ('When thinking is turned on, response pricing is the sum of output tokens and thinking tokens.') || refuter: COD-llm-adapters-2-6: refuter admitted -> medium
entries.root_cause: gemini.py:167-173 reports output_tokens=candidates_token_count and input_tokens=prompt_token_count; google-genai documents thoughts_token_count and tool_use_prompt_token_count as separate billed components, and budget_guard.py:116-133 folds only input+output.
entries.fix_shape: output_tokens = candidates + thoughts; input_tokens = prompt + tool_use_prompt (None-safe). Test: fake usage_metadata with thoughts_token_count=6000, candidates=800 -> adapter usage output_tokens == 6800 and BudgetGuard trips accordingly.

entries.title: POST /llm/chat scrubs adapter options with a four-name denylist while the agent path uses an allowlist, so any new composer control key reaches the provider SDK and TypeErrors the chat stream (the same class already shipped once)
entries.repro: Add any new control key to the composer (streaming.ts wireOptions forwards every option verbatim) -> POST /llm/chat forwards it into the provider SDK -> TypeError: create() got an unexpected keyword argument -> the stream dies with a humanized error. The router's own comment records the live repro of this exact failure: 'research_depth killed a DeepSeek stream' || POST /llm/chat with options {"depth": "deep"}: routers/llm.py:126-130 strips only {research_depth, deepResearchBackend, modelWebSearch, history}, so `depth` rides **adapter_options into the SDK. agent_runtime.py:1363-1366 documents that exact crash ('AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument depth') and fixes it only for the agent path, by popping `depth` (:1368) and then scrubbing everything outside _ADAPTER_OPTION_KEYS (:1381-1385).

entries.title: Delegate runs have no lifecycle state machine: cancel/pause act on any status and rewrite terminal history (done -> cancelled), and resume re-executes a finished run and zeroes its cost
entries.repro: POST /runs/{id}/cancel on a finished run -> 200 and the row flips done -> cancelled 'cancelled by user' (scratch proof P3). POST /runs/{id}/resume on a done run re-executes it and zeroes its cost. pause_run on a done run flips it to paused - the repo's own test does exactly that because it is the only way to exercise pause.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/run_manager.py:291-298 (cancel: no status check), :309-316 (pause: none), :361-366 (resume: only checks a live task), :394-400, sidecar/services/runs_store.py:273-275 (update_run accepts any transition), sidecar/tests/test_run_manager.py:258-266 (test pauses a completed run), sidecar/routers/runs.py:133 (error kind classified by `'already running' in str(exc)`), sidecar/routers/runs.py:119-120 (answer maps the same error to 404 that resume maps to 409) || refuter: COD-runs-durable-delegate-5: refuter admitted -> medium
entries.root_cause: Legal transitions live only in docstrings (models/run.py:28-36); cancel_run/pause_run check nothing, resume_run only checks a live task, update_run writes any status, and the router classifies errors by substring ('already running') mapping it to 404 in answer and 409 in resume.
entries.fix_shape: One transition table enforced in the store as UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status IN (...); rowcount 0 -> typed RunStateError -> 409, RunNotFound -> 404; drop substring matching. Tests: cancel/resume/pause on a done run -> 409 and row unchanged; replace the test that pauses a completed run.

entries.title: The LLM router carries BYOK keys two ways (X-LLM-Key header on /llm/models, JSON body on /llm/chat and /llm/keys/validate) while one docstring says 'never the body'
entries.repro: design (GET /llm/models takes the key as X-LLM-Key header; POST /llm/chat and POST /llm/keys/validate take api_key as a JSON body field - all three in the same 162-line file)
entries.evidence: sidecar/routers/llm.py:52-65, sidecar/routers/llm.py:60-64, sidecar/models/llm.py:243-259, sidecar/models/llm.py:262-269, sidecar/services/llm/base.py:7-11 || refuter: COD-llm-adapters-10: refuter admitted_with_correction -> low
entries.root_cause: Two conventions in one 162-line file (llm.py:52-65 vs models/llm.py:243-269; base.py:7-11 documents the body convention).
entries.fix_shape: Pick one transport (header, matching the BYOK rule) for all three routes, or delete the contradicting clause; add a router test that no response echoes the key.

entries.title: GET /mcp/status reports protocolVersion 2025-06-18 while the live server negotiates 2025-11-25
entries.repro: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52152/mcp/status` -> {"ready":true,"toolCount":36,"endpoint":"/mcp","protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}. `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:52152/mcp/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"x","version":"0"}}}'` -> result.protocolVersion = "2025-11-25". `mcp.types.LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION` in the venv is "2025-11-25".
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:58, sidecar/routers/mcp.py:40, types/mcp.ts:8, types/mcp.ts:104 || refuter: COD-mcp-servers-7: refuter admitted_with_correction -> low
entries.root_cause: mcp_server.py:58 hardcodes the revision; the SDK's LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION moved (types/mcp.ts already says 2025-11-25).
entries.fix_shape: Return mcp.types.LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION and delete the constant; test asserts /mcp/status equals the initialize-negotiated version.

entries.title: Vysted-as-MCP-server returns catalog-tool failures as successful results with an {ok:false} body (isError unset) while Vysted-as-client keys failure off isError
entries.repro: design. mcp_server.py:116-122 converts every handler failure (KeyError, any Exception) into a SUCCESSFUL tool result whose body is {'ok': False, 'error': ...}; nothing in _build_server ever sets isError. Meanwhile openbb_mcp_provider.py:187-190 and sec_filings_provider.py:131-134 treat result['isError'] as THE failure signal.
entries.evidence: sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:120, sidecar/services/mcp_server.py:122, sidecar/services/openbb_mcp_provider.py:187, sidecar/services/sec_filings_provider.py:131 || refuter: COD-mcp-servers-13: refuter admitted_with_correction -> low
entries.root_cause: _make_catalog_tool (mcp_server.py:116-122) converts every handler failure into a success; hand-written tools that raise do set isError, so the server mixes both conventions.
entries.fix_shape: Raise fastmcp ToolError from _make_catalog_tool on failure. Test: a failing catalog tool over MCP returns isError=True.

entries.title: McpClient.call_tool drops structuredContent, so sec_filings_provider's structured-content fallback is dead code
entries.repro: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: stub a session whose call_tool returns an object with isError=False, content=[], structuredContent={'x': 1}; `await McpClient(...).call_tool('t', {})` returns {'isError': False, 'content': []} - structuredContent is gone, so sec_filings_provider._decode_tool_result falls through to `raise ProviderError(... returned no content)`. `mcp.types.CallToolResult.model_fields` is ['meta', 'content', 'structuredContent', 'isError'].

entries.fix_shape: Pass structuredContent through in the return dict and add it to McpToolCallResult in types/mcp.ts (or delete the dead fallback). Test: stub session with structuredContent only -> decoded.

entries.title: ToolKind.mcp_endpoint is documented as MCP-only but the projection rule would set mcp=False for it, so a future mcp_endpoint capability would silently appear nowhere

entries.fix_shape: Delete the mcp_endpoint member until a caller exists (or include it in the projection rule with a parity test).

entries.title: The runs wire contract is documented as camelCase, consumed as snake_case, and papered over by a dual-case serializer; 'cleaning up' _dual_case to the documented contract zeroes cost in the rail
entries.repro: design
entries.evidence: sidecar/routers/runs.py:44-60 (_dual_case emits every key twice 'without a contract negotiation'), sidecar/models/run.py:10-17 (says the wire is camelCase and that types/data.ts mirrors it - no TS mirror of the run models exists), src/lib/delegate-runs.ts:29-38 and :167-172 (RunWire: 'snake_case from the sidecar', reads only spend_usd), docs/SIDECAR_API.md (no runs section) || refuter: COD-runs-durable-delegate-13: refuter admitted -> low
entries.root_cause: runs.py:44-60 emits both spellings; models/run.py:10-17 claims a camelCase wire mirrored in types/data.ts (none exists); RunWire reads only spend_usd.
entries.fix_shape: Pick snake_case, delete _dual_case and the aliases, correct the docstring, add a runs section to SIDECAR_API.md; a router test pins the chosen keys.
